tasks.natural_language: Delete the contents of the /home/mydata/web directory
tasks.original_reference_solution:
---
- name: Delete contents of directory /home/mydata/web
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Delete contets of directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        state: "{{ item }}"
        path: /home/mydata/web
      with_items:
        - absent
        - directory
tasks.proposed_reference_solution:
---
- name: Empty directory while preserving its parent
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: List immediate entries including hidden files and directories
      ansible.builtin.find:
        paths: /home/mydata/web
        file_type: any
        hidden: true
        recurse: false
      register: contents
    - name: Remove each entry while retaining the parent directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item.path }}"
        state: absent
      loop: "{{ contents.files }}"
tasks.rationale: Preserve the FQL for score continuity: DeleteFiles(InPath) asserts every child is a regular file; it does not cover arbitrary directory contents. The supplied playbook deletes/recreates the parent and also fails native lowering for templated state. Do not credit destructive reconstruction as equivalent to preserving the parent. Proposed find/file playbook keeps the parent, handles hidden/directories, and still needs execution validation; no fully faithful corrected FQL is claimed.

tasks.natural_language: For RedHat and Ubuntu, install the lastest version of postfix, backup its default configuration file, and download the configuration file from http://example.com/cfg.ubuntu for Ubuntu and http://example.com/cfg.redhat for RedHat
tasks.original_formal_query: if os is RedHat or os is Ubuntu then install postfix with version=latest; copy postfix configuration file to ?backup. if os is Ubuntu then download postfix configuration file from "http://example.com/cfg.ubuntu". if os is "RedHat" then download postfix configuration file from "http://example.com/cfg.redhat"
tasks.proposed_formal_query: if os is RedHat or os is Ubuntu then install postfix with version=latest; copy postfix configuration file to ?backup. if os is Ubuntu then download postfix configuration file from "http://example.com/cfg.ubuntu". if os is "RedHat" then download postfix configuration file from "http://example.com/cfg.redhat"
tasks.original_reference_solution:
---
- name: Various postfix configuration tasks
  hosts: redhat,ubuntu
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install postfix
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: postfix
        state: latest
    - name: Backup original main.cf
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /etc/postfix/main.cf
        dest: /etc/postfix/main.bak
        force: false
        remote_src: true
    - name: Download main.cf
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "http://example.com/cfg.{{ ansible_distribution | lower }}"
        dest: /etc/postfix/main.cf
        #validate_certs: false
        mode: '644'
        owner: root
        group: root
        force: true
tasks.proposed_reference_solution:

tasks.natural_language: Enable passwordless sudo for a `wheel' group and create an `ansible' user in that group
tasks.original_formal_query: enable passwordless sudo for group=wheel; create user with name=ansible in supplemental groups=wheel
tasks.proposed_formal_query: enable passwordless sudo for group=wheel; create user with name=ansible in supplemental groups=wheel
tasks.original_reference_solution:
---
- name: Enable passwordless sudo for wheel and create an ansible user in that group
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install sudo
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: sudo
        state: present
    - name: Wheel group
      ansible.builtin.group:
        name: wheel
        system: true
        state: present
    - name: Ansible user
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: ansible
        comment: Ansible User
        groups:
          - wheel
        state: present
    - name: Allow group wheel to sudo
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: "/etc/sudoers"
        line: "%wheel        ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL"
        regexp: "^%wheel"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "640"
        state: present
tasks.proposed_reference_solution:
---
- name: Enable passwordless sudo for wheel and create an ansible user in that group
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install sudo
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: sudo
        state: present
    - name: Wheel group
      ansible.builtin.group:
        name: wheel
        system: true
        state: present
    - name: Ansible user
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: ansible
        comment: Ansible User
        groups:
          - wheel
        state: present
    - name: Allow group wheel to sudo
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: "/etc/sudoers"
        line: "%wheel\tALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL"
        regexp: "^%wheel"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "640"
        state: present
tasks.rationale: The NL does not choose primary versus supplemental membership. Accept either/both wheel membership with exactly the requested account and passwordless wheel sudo. Allow a single leading create-group wheel as a prerequisite supported by the supplied reference playbook. Do not equate their full effects; this is an NL-obligation sensitivity. Eight spaces and tab sudoers forms both pass local visudo; the native byte-string comparator is too strict.

tasks.natural_language: For Debian and RedHat, install and start an ssh client and server and generated an ssh key for `fizbaz' at /.ssh/fizbaz_rsa
tasks.original_formal_query: if os is Debian or os is RedHat then install ssh client; install ssh server; start ssh server service; create ssh key for user="fizbaz", name="fizbaz_rsa"
tasks.proposed_formal_query: if os is Debian or os is RedHat then install ssh client; install ssh server; start ssh server service; create ssh key for user="fizbaz" at "/.ssh/fizbaz_rsa"
tasks.original_reference_solution:
---
- name: Install and start ssh client and server and generate an ssh key for fizbaz
  hosts: debian,redhat
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install SSH (Debian)
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name:
          - openssh-client
          - openssh-server
        state: present
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
    - name: Install SSH (RedHat)
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name:
          - openssh-server
          - openssh-clients
        state: present
      when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat"
    - name: Create SSH key
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "fizbaz"
        generate_ssh_key: true
        ssh_key_file: ".ssh/fizbaz_rsa"
    - name: Enable SSH server
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: sshd
        state: started
tasks.proposed_reference_solution:
---
- name: Install and start ssh client and server and generate an ssh key for fizbaz
  hosts: debian,redhat
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install SSH (Debian)
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name:
          - openssh-client
          - openssh-server
        state: present
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
    - name: Install SSH (RedHat)
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name:
          - openssh-server
          - openssh-clients
        state: present
      when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat"
    - name: Create SSH key
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "fizbaz"
        generate_ssh_key: true
        ssh_key_file: "/.ssh/fizbaz_rsa"
    - name: Enable SSH server
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: sshd
        state: started
tasks.rationale: Correct the home-relative reference key to the explicitly stated absolute /.ssh/fizbaz_rsa. Keep exact Debian/RedHat scope and ordered actions; allow equivalent OS branching. The user attribution is consumed/dropped for explicit-path CreateSshKey in the native AST, and starting an SSH client is underspecified; the scoring cannot establish ownership/client behavior. Source intent may instead have meant a home-relative path, requiring author confirmation.
